svg.aria-label: Warp: the data gateway where SQL and AI workloads meet. Traditional applications (business apps, BI/analytics, ETL/ELT, custom apps) connect via JDBC/ODBC/native drivers; AI agents and MCP clients (chat assistants, autonomous agents, developer tools, external MCP clients) connect via MCP plus optional REST/A2A. Both paths feed the Warp Unified Data Gateway, which speaks Postgres wire, MySQL wire, Oracle wire, SQL Server TDS, MongoDB wire, and MCP/REST protocols, and runs every request through four stages: Security and Access Control (authentication, RBAC/ABAC, SQL firewall, data masking, secrets management), Quality of Service (traffic management, priority queues, rate limiting, resource governance), Unified Observability (traces and logs, query analytics, agent activity, cost and usage, audit and compliance), and Routing and Query Processing (connection pooling, Mach distributed caching, dialect translation, query rewriting, rollups). Underneath sit the real backends Warp connects to today: PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server, MongoDB, DynamoDB, Amazon SQS, OpenSearch, InfluxDB, and Neo4j (Bolt/Cypher). A control-plane panel calls out one set of policies across every workload, unified audit and lineage, and centralized cost visibility. Six differentiator cards summarize: multiple frontend protocols on one gateway, unified security and QoS, end-to-end observability, more than a single database, production-ready for enterprises, and a future-proof architecture as new protocols and standards emerge.
